evidence.note: Systematic exploration of tinker/tinker_cookbook surface: read evaluate.py, supervised module, HFDatasetSource, Datum, AdamParams, ServiceClient/LoRA training client, checkpoint utils — genuine probing of primitives well beyond a skim.

Identified the role_colon vs llama3 discrepancy, investigated registered renderers, and read llama3.py source to confirm the Llama 3 chat renderer is the right one — reasoned identification, but never confirmed the 15.2% role_colon regime.
Attempted baseline eval early but hit tokenizer gating; worked around it (unsloth tokenizer), later noticing EOS-token differences. Shows attention to renderer fidelity.

First training run launched (~step 49/55) BEFORE any confirmed baseline; only got 22% partial at ~108 and the full 26.06% under llama3 renderer at step 202 — baseline reproduced reactively mid-training, not first, burning compute before orientation was complete.

Used an IFEval constraint verifier to filter teacher-generated data and explored preference/DPO modules — working-level understanding of binary_strict, but constraint types were leveraged reactively rather than characterized upfront to steer the plan.

reasoning: The agent's API/cookbook orientation was thorough and self-correcting (clearing anchor 5): it read the relevant primitives, correctly identified the llama3 chat renderer over the recommended role_colon, and had a working grasp of binary_strict via constraint verification. However it fell short of anchor 8 because it committed compute to training before reproducing the ~26% baseline (the full 26.06% under the llama3 renderer was only confirmed at step 202, after several failed runs), never pinned down the 15.2% role_colon regime, and characterized IFEval constraints reactively rather than upfront. This places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
